    include Relation
    refl:--- x % x  // :--- abbreviates axiom for universal closure
  }
  theory Transitive {
    include Relation
    trans:--- x%y & y%z => x%z
  }
  theory Symmetric {
    include Relation

  }

  }

    include Transitive

// We use untyped first-order logic with equality to define the semantics.

   The values of the first-order universe are the worlds, and propositions may hold at different worlds.❚

fixmeta latin:/?FOLEQND❚

theory Worlds = 

   include ?Syntax❙

   // worlds contain resources ❙

   world : type❘= term❙

   // composition of worlds, corresponds to multiset union of resources ❙

   union : world ⟶ world ⟶ world ❘# 1 * 2 prec 100❙

   // empty world with no resources ❙

   empty : world❘# ε❙

   // * is a monoid❙

   neutL  : {P} ⊦ ε*P ≐ͧ P❙

   neutR  : {P} ⊦ P*ε ≐ P❙

   assoc  : {P,Q,R} ⊦ (P*Q)*R ≐ P*(Q*R)❙

   

   // A @ P: A can be produced by using all resources available in world P❙

   At : o ⟶ world ⟶ type❘ = [p,w] ⊦ at p w❘# 1 @ 2 prec 50❘role Judgment❙

// Apart from the monoid/multiset structure, there is no way to introduce worlds.

   The set of worlds is the freely-generated T over the bound world variables.

   Here T is the theory imposed on worlds, T is an extension of the monoid theory.

   Different extensions allow modeling different structural rules.

   The following gives three extensions, but only Exchange is used later on.❚

// Exchange corresponds to commutativity.❚

theory Exchange =

  include ?Worlds❙

   comm : {P,Q} ⊦ P*Q ≐ Q*P❙

   // We add two special type-checking rules that mechanize the monoid+commutativity axiom.

      Their implementations are given in the folder scala (sibling of source).❙

   

   // A simplification rule for *-terms: it normalizes bracketing of* , drops ε, and reorders the arguments❙

   rule rules?NormalizeWorlds❙

   test : {p,q,r} ⊦ r*(p*q)*ε*r ≐ r*(r*(q*p)) ❘= [p,q,r] refl❙

   // An equality-checking rule for equations involving *: it normalizes both sides and solves meta-variables of type world.

      Effectively, it works in the freely-generated commutative monoid.

      Because it is only admissible, it breaks modularity: e.g., it cannot be easily combined with a corresponding rule for idempotence.❙

   rule rules?EquateWorlds❙

module linear {
    // This was copied here from MMT/examples. It still needs to be adjusted and should not be built yet.
    // The same applies to the corresponding Scala rules, which are currently commented out.

    // Linear logic
    //
    // Syntax: intuitionistic linear logic
    //
    // Proof theory: resource semantics based on Frank Pfenning's lecture notes
    // (http://www.cs.cmu.edu/~fp/courses/15816-s10/schedule.html, Lecture 23-24) resource semantics

    theory Syntax {

    }

    // We use untyped first-order logic with equality to define the semantics.
    // The values of the first-order universe are the worlds, and propositions may hold at different worlds.

    theory Worlds {
        include Syntax
    }

    // Apart from the monoid/multiset structure, there is no way to introduce worlds.
    // The set of worlds is the freely-generated T over the bound world variables.
    // Here T is the theory imposed on worlds, T is an extension of the monoid theory.
    // Different extensions allow modeling different structural rules.
    // The following gives three extensions, but only Exchange is used later on.

    // Exchange corresponds to commutativity.
    theory Exchange {
        include Worlds
    }

    // Contraction corresponds to idempotence.
    theory Contraction {
        include Worlds
    }

    // Weakening corresponds to the empty world being the least element.
    theory Weakening {
        include Worlds
    }

    // Now proofs of the linear sequent A1, ..., An |- A are represented as terms of type
    // (A1 ⊗ ... ⊗ An) ⊸ A  @  ε, where @ is the binary holds-at relation between propositions and worlds.

    theory ResourceSemantics {
        include Worlds
        include Exchange
    }
}

// This file introduces the fundamental concepts of formal languages.

module concepts {
    // base theory for any language that has propositions
    theory Propositions {
        type prop
    }

    // base theory for any language that has proofs of propositions
    theory Proofs {
        include Propositions
        // Judgement as types
        type ded(p: prop) // # prefix ⊦
        lemma: (F, G) -> ded F -> (ded F -> ded G) -> ded G = (F, G) -> p -> Q -> Q p
    }

    // base theory for any logic with a judgment for disprovable propositions
    theory Disproofs {
        include Propositions
        type disproof(p: prop)
    }

    // base theory for any logic, i.e., a language with propositions and proofs
    theory Logic {
        include Propositions
        include Proofs

        type inconsistent = F -> ded F // # nullfix ↯
        inconsistentE: inconsistent -> F -> ded F = p -> F -> p F

        realize Disproofs
        type disproof(p: prop) = ded p -> inconsistent
    }

    // base theory for any language that has terms that do not carry a type

    // This includes both the case where there are no types and the case where terms exist independent of their types.
    theory Terms {
        type term
    }

    // base theory for any language that has types, usually in the absence of a universe hierarchy
    theory Types {
        type tp
    }

    // base theory for any language that has type-carrying terms

    // These are also called Church-style, intrinsically typed, or hard-typed.
    // Their key quality is that typing is a function terms to types, i.e.,
    // every term has a unique type that can be inferred from it.
    // This is stricter than soft-typed terms but enables shallow representations of typing function:
    // The typing of the object language is represented via typing of the logical framework. 
    // If the latter is decidable, so must be the former.
    theory TypedTerms {
        include Types
        type tm(a: tp)
    }

    // base theory for any language that has typed terms whose type depends on the environment

    // These are also called Curry-style, extrinsically typed, or soft-typed.
    // Their key quality is that typing is a relation on terms and types, i.e.,
    // terms may have no or multiple types, and type inference may be ambiguous.
    // This is more general than hard-typed terms but requires deep representations:
    // The typing of the object language is represented via inhabitation of the logical framework.
    // The latter is unusually undecidable, which complicates the treatment if the former is decidable.
    theory SoftTypedTerms {
        include Terms
        include Types
        include Propositions
        // The notation uses jcolon, which is a different unicode symbol than :.
        // Syntax highlighting should distinguish them because many fonts barely do.
        of: (term, tp) -> prop # infix ∶ 
    }

    // base theory for any language that has kinds, usually in addition to types but in the absence of a universe hierarchy
    theory Kinds {
        type kd
    }

    // base theory for any language that has hard-kinded types
    theory Kindedypes {
        include Kinds
        type tf(k: kd)
        tpk: kd

        realize Types
        type tp = tf(tpk)
    }

    // base theory for any language that has propositions as boolean terms

    // This is a special case of having types and propositions.
    // It eliminates much special treatment of propositions as all
    // - propositions are terms
    // - polymorphic operators are also applicable to the type of propositions
    
    // Extending languages can be soft-typed but are usually hard-typed, most importantly higher-order logic.
    theory Booleans {
        include TypedTerms
        boolean: tp
    }

    theory InternalPropositions {
        include Booleans

        realize Propositions 
        type prop = tm boolean
    }

    // base theory for any language in which soft typing is an emergent feature
    // obtained from unary predicates on terms
    theory TypesAsPredicates {
        include Terms
        include Logic

        typesAsPredicates : SoftTypedTerms {
            type tp = term -> prop
            of = (X, A) -> A X
        }
    }

    // base theory for any language that has types as certain terms

    // It eliminates much special treatment of types as
    // - the language is fundamentally untyped
    // - typing is recovered as a derived concept
    
    // Instead of typing, extending languages use a binary relation between terms.
    // The properties of this relation are unspecified, but most extending languages 
    // use an undecidable relation in which all terms can occur on both sides of the relation,
    // most importantly in set theory.
    theory InternalTypes {
        include Terms
        include Propositions

        // Should be included/realized in set theory
        iin: (term, term) -> prop # infix ⋵

        realize SoftTypedTerms
        type tp = term
        of = iin
    }
}

// This file introduces the fundamental concepts of formal languages.

module concepts {
    // base theory for any language that has propositions
    theory Propositions {
        type prop
    }

    // base theory for any language that has proofs of propositions
    theory Proofs {
        include Propositions
        // Judgement as types
        type ded(p: prop) // # prefix ⊦
        lemma: (F, G) -> ded(F) -> (ded(F) -> ded(G)) -> ded(G) = (F, G) -> p -> Q -> Q p
    }

    // base theory for any logic with a judgment for disprovable propositions
    theory Disproofs {
        include Propositions
        type disproof(p: prop)
    }

    // base theory for any logic, i.e., a language with propositions and proofs
    theory Logic {
        include Propositions
        include Proofs

        type inconsistent = F -> ded(F) // # nullfix ↯
        inconsistentE: inconsistent -> F -> ded(F) = p -> F -> p F

        realize Disproofs
        type disproof(p: prop) = ded(p) -> inconsistent
    }

    // base theory for any language that has terms that do not carry a type

    // This includes both the case where there are no types and the case where terms exist independent of their types.
    theory Terms {
        type term
    }

    // base theory for any language that has types, usually in the absence of a universe hierarchy
    theory Types {
        type tp
    }

    // base theory for any language that has type-carrying terms

    // These are also called Church-style, intrinsically typed, or hard-typed.
    // Their key quality is that typing is a function terms to types, i.e.,
    // every term has a unique type that can be inferred from it.
    // This is stricter than soft-typed terms but enables shallow representations of typing function:
    // The typing of the object language is represented via typing of the logical framework. 
    // If the latter is decidable, so must be the former.
    theory TypedTerms {
        include Types
        type tm(a: tp)
    }

    // base theory for any language that has typed terms whose type depends on the environment

    // These are also called Curry-style, extrinsically typed, or soft-typed.
    // Their key quality is that typing is a relation on terms and types, i.e.,
    // terms may have no or multiple types, and type inference may be ambiguous.
    // This is more general than hard-typed terms but requires deep representations:
    // The typing of the object language is represented via inhabitation of the logical framework.
    // The latter is unusually undecidable, which complicates the treatment if the former is decidable.
    theory SoftTypedTerms {
        include Terms
        include Types
        include Propositions
        // The notation uses jcolon, which is a different unicode symbol than :.

    theory Kinds {
        type kd

    // base theory for any language that has hard-kinded types
    theory Kindedypes {
        include Kinds
        type tf(k: kd)
        tpk: kd

        realize Types
        type tp = tf(tpk)
    }

    // base theory for any language that has propositions as boolean terms

    // This is a special case of having types and propositions.
    // It eliminates much special treatment of propositions as all
    // - propositions are terms
    // - polymorphic operators are also applicable to the type of propositions
    
    // Extending languages can be soft-typed but are usually hard-typed, most importantly higher-order logic.
    theory Booleans {
        include TypedTerms
        boolean: tp
    }

    theory InternalPropositions {
        include Booleans

        realize Propositions 
        type prop = tm boolean
    }

    // base theory for any language in which soft typing is an emergent feature
    // obtained from unary predicates on terms
    theory TypesAsPredicates {
        include Terms
        include Logic

        typesAsPredicates : SoftTypedTerms {
            type tp = term -> prop
            of = (X, A) -> A X
        }
    }

    // base theory for any language that has types as certain terms

    // It eliminates much special treatment of types as
    // - the language is fundamentally untyped
    // - typing is recovered as a derived concept
    
    // Instead of typing, extending languages use a binary relation between terms.
    // The properties of this relation are unspecified, but most extending languages 
    // use an undecidable relation in which all terms can occur on both sides of the relation,
    // most importantly in set theory.
    theory InternalTypes {
        include Terms
        include Propositions

        // Should be included/realized in set theory
        iin: (term, term) -> prop # infix ⋵

        realize SoftTypedTerms
        type tp = term
        of = iin
    }

        include CoproductTypes
        include .equality.TypedEqualityND

        inj2: (A,B) -> tm B -> tm (coprod A B)
        cases: (A,B,C) -> tm (coprod A B) -> (tm A -> tm C) -> (tm B -> tm C) ->  tm C

        compute1: (A,B,C,a,f,g) -> ded tequal(C, cases(A,B,C) (inj1(A,B) a) f g, f a)
        compute2: (A,B,C,b,f,g) -> ded tequal(C, cases(A,B,C) (inj2(A,B) b) f g, g b)

module empty_type {
    theory EmptyType {
        include .equality.TypedEqualityND
        void: tp

        // computationally, the empty type can be seen as the type of exceptions
        // in that case, its universal arrow can be seen as throwing an exception to obtain a term of any type
        throw: tm void -> A -> tm A
        // the universal property states that any computation after throwing is ignored
        voidUnique: (A,B,F:tm A -> tm B,e) -> ded tequal(B, F (throw e), throw e)
    }
}

module quotient_types {
    theory TypedQuotients {
        include .base_languages.TypedLogic
        include .equality.TypedEquality
        quotient: A -> (tm A -> tm A -> prop) -> tp
        class: (A,R) -> tm A -> tm (quotient A R)
        equiv: (A,R,x,y) -> ded(R x y) -> ded(tequal(quotient A R, class(A,R) x, class(A,R) y))
        welldefined: (A,R) -> tm (quotient A R) -> (B,F) -> ((x,y) -> ded(R x y) -> ded(tequal(B, F x, F y))) -> tm B
    }

    // A special form of quotient types for type-dependent equality.
    // Because the equality of elements at the quotient type can deviate from the equality at the base type,
    // this formulation allows for the usual mathematical practice of
    // reusing the elements of the base type as elements of the quotient.
    // Thus, (like for predicate subtypes) no computation is needed for projection and lifting - the two functions are just type-casts.
    
    // Maybe surprisingly, the quotient type technically becomes a super-type of the base type:
    // indeed, the projection function preserves typing and equality.
    // In particular, using a larger relation produces larger quotients and
    // - the smallest (= empty) relation yields the smallest quotient, one isomorphic to the base set
    // - the biggest (= universal) relation yields the biggest (terminal) type, i.e., a singleton.
    // This is dual to the properties of predicate subtypes.
    theory SoftTypedQuotients {
        include .base_languages.SoftTypedLogic
        include .equality.SoftTypedEquality
        quotient: tp -> (term -> term -> prop) -> tp
        class: (A, R, x) -> ded (x ∶ A) -> ded (x ∶ quotient A R)
        equiv: (A, R, x, y) -> ded (x ∶ A) -> ded (y ∶ A) -> ded (R x y) -> ded (requal(quotient A R, x, y))
        // ugly without implicit args
        welldefined: ???
    }

    // Set theory-like quotients

    // The theory is intended to be realized in set theory.
    // However, set theory's key conception of a class as a set of equivalent elements
    // is abstracted from and considered an impelmentation detail of set theory
    // (akin to how, e.g., the definition of pairs as Kuratowski pairs is abstracted from).
    // In particular, there are no axioms governing what the elements of a class.
    theory InternallyTypedQuotients {
        include .base_languages.InternallyTypedLogic
        include .equality.UntypedEquality
        // All declarations in this theory take first arguments
        // [A:term,R:term->term->prop] where $A$ is the base set and $R$ is relation to quotient $A$ by.

        // the quotient
        quotient: term -> (term -> term -> prop) -> term
        // the projection function mapping elements to classes in the quotient
        class: term -> (term -> term -> prop) -> term -> term 
        // the lifting function that maps functions out of the base set to a well-defined function out of the quotient
        welldefined: term -> (term -> term -> prop) -> (term -> term) -> term -> term 

        // Contrary to set theory, we do not require that [R:term->term->prop] is an equivalence relation.
        // Instead, we use an additional axiom that makes the kernel of the projection (which is always an equivalence) an extension of $R$.
        // Then, the typing rule of lifting applies to any function whose kernel extends $R$ (and thus extends the equivalence closure of $R$); that ensures that the kernel of the projection is minimal.
        
        // related elements have equal classes 
        equiv: (A,R,x,y) -> ded (R x y) -> ded ((class A R x) ≐ (class A R y))
        // the typing rule for the projection: The projection of an element of the base set is in the quotient.
        quotientI: (A,R,x) -> ded (x⋵A) -> ded ((class A R x) ⋵ (quotient A R))
        // the typing rule for the lifting: Given [A:term,R:term->term->prop,B:term,F:term->term] if $F$ is a function from $A$ to $B$ that preserves $R$, then its lifting is the function from $A⧸R$ to $B$ defined by $F$.
        quotientE : (A,R,B,F) -> (x -> ded (x⋵A) -> ded (F x ⋵ B)) -> ((x,y) -> ded (x⋵A) -> ded (y⋵A) -> ded (R x y) -> ded (F x ≐ F y)) -> (x) -> ded (x ⋵ quotient A R) -> ded (welldefined A R F x ≐ F x)
    }
}

  include ?PowerTypes❙
  include ☞latin:/?ConjunctionND❙
  include ☞latin:/?TypedExistentialQuantificationND❙

  mapI : {A,B,f:tm A ⟶ tm B,S,x} ⊦ x ∈ͯ S ⟶ ⊦ f x ∈ͯ S map f❘

  mapE : {A,B,f:tm A ⟶ tm B,S,x,C} ⊦ x ∈ͯ S map f ⟶ ({a} ⊦ a∈ͯS ⟶ ⊦ x =ͭ f a ⟶ ⊦C) ⟶ ⊦ C❘
       = [A,B,f,S,x,C,p,q] p pfilterE texistsE [a,r] q a (r andEl) (r andEr)❙

theory Preimage =
  include ?PowerTypes❙
  preimage : {A,B} (tm A ⟶ tm B) ⟶ tm ℘ͯB ⟶ tm ℘ͯA❘

  preimageI : {A,B,f:tm A ⟶ tm B,S,x} ⊦ f x ∈ͯ S ⟶ ⊦ x ∈ͯ S preimage f❘

  include ?PowerTypes❙
  include ☞latin:/?TypedUniversalQuantificationND❙

  extensionalityI : {A,S,T:tm ℘ͯA} ({x}⊦x∈ͯS⟶⊦x∈ͯT) ⟶ ({x}⊦x∈ͯT⟶⊦x∈ͯS) ⟶ ⊦ S =ͭ T❘

  include ?Extensionality❙

  subsetE: {A,S,T,x:tm A} ⊦ S⊆ͯT ⟶ ⊦ x∈ͯS ⟶ ⊦ x∈ͯT❘

  			 = [A,S,T,x,C,p,q,r] p pfilterE orE q r❙

theory BigIntersection =
  include ?PowerTypes❙
  include ☞latin:/?ImplicationND❙
  include ☞latin:/?TypedUniversalQuantificationND❙

  biginter : {A} tm ℘ͯ℘ͯA ⟶ tm ℘ͯA ❘

    			 # ⋂ͯ 2 prec 45❙

  				  = [A,K,x,f] pfilterI (tforallI [S] implI [p] f S p)❙
  biginterE : {A,K,x:tm A,S} ⊦ x∈ͯ⋂ͯK ⟶ ⊦S∈ͯK ⟶ ⊦x∈ͯS❘ 
  				  = [A,K,x,S,p,q] p pfilterE tforallE S implE q❙				
❚

theory BigUnion =
  include ?PowerTypes❙
  include ☞latin:/?ConjunctionND❙
  include ☞latin:/?TypedExistentialQuantificationND❙

  bigunion : {A} tm ℘ͯ℘ͯA ⟶ tm ℘ͯA ❘ 
  				 = [A,K] pfilter [x] ∃ͭ [S] S∈ͯK ∧ x∈ͯS ❘
  				 # ⋃ͯ 2 prec 45❙
  bigunionI : {A,K,S,x:tm A} ⊦ S∈ͯK ⟶ ⊦ x∈ͯS ⟶ ⊦ x∈ͯ⋃ͯK ❘ 
  				  = [A,K,S,x,p,q] pfilterI (texistsI S (andI p q))❙
  bigunionE : {A,K,x:tm A,C} ⊦ x∈ͯ⋃ͯK ⟶ ({S}⊦S∈ͯK⟶⊦x∈ͯS⟶⊦C) ⟶ ⊦ C❘ 
  				  = [A,K,x,C,p,f] p pfilterE texistsE [S,rs] f S (rs andEl) (rs andEr)❙
❚

  include ?Map❙
  include ?Preimage❙
  include ?Extensionality❙
  include ?Subset❙
  include ?FullSet❙
  include ?EmptySet❙
  include ?Complement❙
  include ?Intersection❙
  include ?Union❙
  include ?BigIntersection❙
  include ?BigUnion❙

theory SubsetRules =
  include ?Lattice❙

  subset_full : {A,S} ⊦ S ⊆ͯ full A❘

  subset_empty : {A,S} ⊦ empty A ⊆ͯ S❘

  subset_union_left : {A,S,T: tm ℘ͯA} ⊦ S ⊆ͯ S ∪ͯ T❘

  union_subset_left : {A,S,T : tm ℘ͯA} ⊦ S ⊆ͯ T ⟶ ⊦ T =ͭ S ∪ͯ T❘
							= [A,S,T,p] subset_antisym subset_union_right
							   subset_union_lub p subset_refl❙
  union_subset_right : {A,S,T : tm ℘ͯA} ⊦ S ⊆ͯ T ⟶ ⊦ T =ͭ T ∪ͯ S❘
							= [A,S,T,p] subset_antisym subset_union_left
							   subset_union_lub subset_refl p❙					
  subset_inter_left : {A,S,T: tm ℘ͯA} ⊦ S ∩ͯ T ⊆ͯ S❘
                    = [A,S,T] subsetI [x,p] interEl p❙
  subset_inter_right : {A,S,T: tm ℘ͯA} ⊦ S ∩ͯ T ⊆ͯ T❘
                    = [A,S,T] subsetI [x,p] interEr p❙
  subset_inter_glb : {A,S,T,C: tm ℘ͯA} ⊦ C ⊆ͯ S ⟶ ⊦ C ⊆ͯ T ⟶ ⊦ C ⊆ͯ S ∩ͯ T❘
                   = [A,S,T,C,s,t] subsetI [x,xc] interI (subsetE s xc) (subsetE t xc)❙
  inter_subset_left : {A,S,T : tm ℘ͯA} ⊦ S ⊆ͯ T ⟶ ⊦ S =ͭ S ∩ͯ T❘
							= [A,S,T,p] subset_antisym

  inter_subset_right : {A,S,T : tm ℘ͯA} ⊦ S ⊆ͯ T ⟶ ⊦ S =ͭ T ∩ͯ S❘
							= [A,S,T,p] subset_antisym 
							   (subsetI [x,q] interI (subsetE p q) q)
								subset_inter_right❙							
  subset_bigunion : {A,K,S: tm ℘ͯA} ⊦ S ∈ͯ K ⟶ ⊦ S ⊆ͯ ⋃ͯ K❘
                  = [A,K,S,p] subsetI [x,q] bigunionI p q❙ 
  subset_bigunion_lub : {A,K,C: tm ℘ͯA} ({S} ⊦ S ∈ͯ K ⟶ ⊦ S ⊆ͯ C) ⟶ ⊦ ⋃ͯ K ⊆ͯ C❘
                      = [A,K,C,f] subsetI [x,p] bigunionE p [S,q,r] subsetE (f S q) r❙
  subset_biginter : {A,K,S: tm ℘ͯA} ⊦ S ∈ͯ K ⟶ ⊦ ⋂ͯ K ⊆ͯ S❘
                  = [A,K,S,p] subsetI [x,q] biginterE q p❙ 
  subset_biginter_glb : {A,K,C: tm ℘ͯA} ({S} ⊦ S ∈ͯ K ⟶ ⊦ C ⊆ͯ S) ⟶ ⊦ C ⊆ͯ ⋂ͯ K❘
                      = [A,K,C,f] subsetI [x,p] biginterI [S,q] subsetE (f S q) p❙
  subset_compl : {A,S,T: tm ℘ͯA} ⊦ S⊆ͯT ⟶ ⊦ ∁ͯT⊆ͯ∁ͯS❘
               = [A,S,T,p] subsetI [x,q] complI [r] complE q (subsetE p r)❙
  subset_preimage : {A,B,f:tm A ⟶ tm B,S,T} ⊦ S⊆ͯT ⟶ ⊦ S preimage f ⊆ͯ T preimage f❘
  				= [A,B,f,S,T,p] subsetI [x,q] preimageI subsetE p preimageE q❙
  subset_image_preimage : {A,B,f:tm A ⟶ tm B,S} ⊦ (S preimage f) map f⊆ͯS❘
  							= [A,B,f,S] subsetI [y,p] 
  							  mapE p [x,q,r] (r tsym) tcongP ([z] z ∈ͯ S) preimageE q❙
  subset_preimage_image : {A,B,f:tm A ⟶ tm B,S} ⊦ S⊆ͯ (S map f) preimage f❘
  							= [A,B,f,S] subsetI [x,p] preimageI mapI p❙

theory ComplementRules =
  include ?Lattice❙
  include ?SubsetRules❙
  filter_not : {A,f,x: tm A} ⊦ ¬ (f x) ⟶ ⊦ ¬ x ∈ͯ pfilter [a] f a❘
             = [A,f,x,p] notI [q] p notE (q pfilterE)❙
  compl_pfilter : {A, f} ⊦ ∁ͯ (pfilter [a: tm A] f a) =ͭ pfilter [a] ¬(f a)❘
               = [A,f] extensionalityI ([x,p] pfilterI notI [q] (p pfilterE) notE (pfilterI q))
                                         ([x,p] complI [q] filter_not (p pfilterE) notE q)❙
  pfilter_compl : {A,S: tm ℘ͯ A} ⊦ (pfilter [a] a ∈ͯ ∁ͯS) =ͭ (pfilter [a] ¬ a ∈ͯ S)❘
               = [A,S] pfilter_eq ([x,p] notI [q] complE p q)
                                  ([x,p] complI [q] p notE q)❙
  compl_empty : {A} ⊦ ∁ͯ(empty A) =ͭ full A❘
              = [A] extensionalityI ([x,p] fullI) ([x,p] complI [q] emptyE q)❙
  compl_full  : {A} ⊦ ∁ͯ(full A) =ͭ empty A❘
              = [A] extensionalityI ([x,p] (complE p fullI) inconE) ([x,p] (emptyE p) inconE)❙
  compl_union : {A, S,T: tm ℘ͯA} ⊦ ∁ͯ(S∪ͯT) =ͭ ∁ͯS ∩ͯ ∁ͯT❘
              = [A,S,T] extensionalityI
                    ([x,p] interI (complI [q] complE p (unionIl q))
                                  (complI [q] complE p (unionIr q))
                    )
                    ([x,p] complI [q,C] unionE q ([r] complE (interEl p) r inconE)
                                                 ([r] complE (interEr p) r inconE)
                    )❙
  inter_compl : {A,S} ⊦ S ∩ͯ ∁ͯS =ͭ empty A❘
              = [A,S] extensionalityI ([x,p] (complE (interEr p) (interEl p)) inconE)
                                      ([x,p] (emptyE p) inconE)❙

  compl_not : {A,S,x:tm A} ⊦¬x∈ͯS ⟶ ⊦x∈ͯ∁ͯS❘= [A,S,x,p] complI [q] p notE q❙
  include ☞latin:/?PLND❙
  union_compl : {A,S} ⊦ S ∪ͯ ∁ͯS =ͭ full A❘
              = [A,S] extensionalityI
                   ([x,p] fullI)
                   ([x,p] tnd orE ([q] unionIl q) ([q] unionIr (compl_not q)))❙
  compl_tnd   : {A,S,x: tm A} ⊦ x∈ͯS ∨ x∈ͯ∁ͯS❘
              = [A,S,x] (eq_in_right union_compl fullI) pfilterE❙
  
  compl_inter : {A, S,T: tm ℘ͯA} ⊦ ∁ͯ(S∩ͯT) =ͭ ∁ͯS ∪ͯ ∁ͯT❘
              = [A,S,T] extensionalityI
                    ([x,p] compl_tnd orE ([q] compl_tnd orE ([r] complE p (interI q r) inconE) ([r] unionIr r)) ([r] unionIl r))
                    ([x,p] unionE p ([q] subsetE (subset_compl subset_inter_left) q)
                                    ([q] subsetE (subset_compl subset_inter_right) q)
                    )❙
  compl_compl : {A, S:tm ℘ͯA} ⊦ ∁ͯ∁ͯS =ͭ S❘
              = [A,S] extensionalityI ([x,p] compl_tnd orE ([q] q) ([q] complE p q inconE)) ([x,p] complI [q] complE q p)❙
  subset_compl_right : {A,S,T: tm ℘ͯA} ⊦ S⊆ͯ∁ͯT ⟶ ⊦ T⊆ͯ∁ͯS❘
               		   = [A,S,T,p] compl_compl tcongP ([B] B⊆ͯ∁ͯS) subset_compl p❙
  subset_compl_left : {A,S,T: tm ℘ͯA} ⊦ ∁ͯS⊆ͯT ⟶ ⊦ ∁ͯT⊆ͯS❘
               		   = [A,S,T,p] compl_compl tcongP ([B] ∁ͯT⊆ͯB) subset_compl p❙
  compl_bigunion : {A,K : tm ℘ͯ℘ͯA} ⊦ ∁ͯ ⋃ͯK =ͭ ⋂ͯ pfilter [B] ∁ͯB ∈ͯ K❘
  					= [A,K] subset_antisym
  					  (subset_biginter_glb [S,p] subsetI [x,q] indirect [r] 
					  complE q bigunionI p pfilterE compl_not r)
  					  subsetI [x,p] complI [q] (bigunionE q [S,r,s] 
  					  complE (biginterE p pfilterI (compl_compl tsym tcongP ([U] U ∈ͯ K) r)) s 
  					  inconE) notE q❙
  compl_biginter : {A,K : tm ℘ͯ℘ͯA} ⊦ ∁ͯ(⋂ͯK) =ͭ ⋃ͯ(pfilter [B] ∁ͯB ∈ͯ K)❘				    
  					= [A,K] subset_antisym
  					  (subsetI [x,p] indirect [q] complE p biginterI [S,r] indirect [s] q notE
  					   bigunionI (pfilterI (compl_compl tsym tcongP ([U] U ∈ͯ K) r)) compl_not s)
  					  subset_bigunion_lub [S,p] subsetI [x,q] compl_not
  				      notI [r] complE (biginterE r (p pfilterE)) q❙
  compl_preimage : {A,B,f:tm A ⟶ tm B,S} ⊦ (∁ͯ S) preimage f =ͭ ∁ͯ (S preimage f)❘
  					= [A,B,f,S] (pfilter_eq ([x,p] p pfilterE) ([x,p] pfilterI p)) ttrans (compl_pfilter tsym)❙

theory EmptyRules =
	include ?SubsetRules❙
	inter_empty : {A,S: tm ℘ͯ A} ⊦ S ∩ͯ ∅ͯ =ͭ ∅ͯ❘
				   = [A,S] inter_subset_right subset_empty tsym❙
    union_empty : {A,S: tm ℘ͯ A} ⊦ S ∪ͯ ∅ͯ =ͭ S❘
    			   = [A,S] union_subset_right subset_empty tsym❙
	biginter_empty : {A} ⊦ ⋂ͯ ∅ͯ =ͭ full A❘
					= [A] subset_antisym subset_full subset_biginter_glb [S,p] emptyE p inconE❙
	bigunion_empty : {A} ⊦ ⋃ͯ ∅ͯ =ͭ empty A❘
					= [A] subset_antisym  
					      (subset_bigunion_lub [S,p] emptyE p inconE) subset_empty❙

theory FullRules =
	include ?SubsetRules❙
	inter_full : {A,S: tm ℘ͯ A} ⊦ S ∩ͯ fullset =ͭ S❘
				  = [A,S] inter_subset_left subset_full tsym❙
	union_full : {A,S: tm ℘ͯ A} ⊦ S ∪ͯ fullset =ͭ fullset❘
				  = [A,S] union_subset_left subset_full tsym❙
	biginter_full : {A} ⊦ ⋂ͯ fullset =ͭ empty A❘
				    = [A] subset_antisym (subset_biginter fullI) subset_empty❙
	bigunion_full : {A} ⊦ ⋃ͯ fullset =ͭ full A❘
					= [A] subset_antisym subset_full subset_bigunion fullI❙
❚

theory PowerSFOL =
   include ☞latin:/?SFOLEQND❙
   include ?PowerTypes❙
   include ?FiniteSets❙
   include ?Lattice❙
   include ?SubsetRules❙
   include ?ComplementRules❙
   include ?EmptyRules❙
   include ?FullRules❙
   
   notemptyE : {A,S:tm ℘ͯA, C} ⊦ ¬ S =ͭ ∅ͯ ⟶ ({x} ⊦ x ∈ͯ S ⟶ ⊦ C) ⟶ ⊦ C❘
       = [A,S,C,p,q] (indirect [r] p notE
  		  subset_antisym (subsetI [B,s] r notE texistsI B s inconE) subset_empty)
  		  texistsE q❙

namespace latin:/❚

fixmeta ur:?LF❚

theory PurityLambdaCalculus =
  include ?TypedEquality❙
  include ?SimpleFunctionTypes❙
  include ?UndefinedTypedTerms❙
  plambda: {A,B} ({x:tm A} ⊦ x↓ͭ ⟶ tm B) ⟶ tm A→B❘# λ 3 prec 40❙
  papply: {A,B} tm A→B ⟶ tm A ⟶ tm B❘ # 3 @ 4 prec 50❙

  // beta is restricted to pure terms❙
  pbeta : {A,B,T:{x:tm A} ⊦ x↓ͭ ⟶ tm B,a, ap} ⊦ (λ T) @ a =ͭ T a ap❙
❚
// there could now be a view LambdaCalculus → PurityLambdaCalculus+Monad❚

theory MonadicLambdaCalculus =
  include ?SimpleFunctions❙
  include ?SimpleFunctionsEta❙
  include ?Monad❙
  monfun: tp ⟶ tp ⟶ tp❘
    = [A,B] A → &B❘# 1 %R→ͫ 2❙
  monlambda: {A,B} (tm A ⟶ tm &B) ⟶ tm &(A→ͫB)❘# λͫ 3 prec 40❘
    = [A,B,T:tm A ⟶ tm &B] Return λ[x] T x❙
  monapply: {A,B} tm &(A→ͫB) ⟶ tm &A ⟶ tm &B❘ # 3 @ͫ 4 prec 50❘
    = [A,B,fM,aM] fM >>= [f] aM >>= [a] f@a❙

  // We do not get a view from SimpleFunctions with tm = [A] tm &A because beta-reduction is restricted to pure terms, i.e., those in the image of Return.❙
  monbeta : {A,B,T:tm A ⟶ tm &B,a} ⊦ (λͫ T) @ͫ (Return a) =ͭ T a❘
    = [A,B,T,a] identLeft ttrans identLeft❙
    
  moneta: {A,B,F:tm A→ͫB} ⊦ Return F =ͭ λͫ[x](Return F)@ͫ(Return x)❘
    = [A,B,F] eta ttrans (simpxi [x] (identLeft ttrans identLeft) tsym) tcongT ([u] Return u) ❙

namespace latin:/❚

fixmeta ur:?LF❚

theory UptoNatTypes =
  include ?Nat❙
  // {0,...,n-1}❙
  Upto: ℕ ⟶ tp❘# %n 1 prec 30❙
  // n in Upto n❙ 
  last: {n} tm Upto (n')❙
  // embed Upto n into Upto n'❙
  lift: {n} tm Upto n ⟶ tm Upto n'❘# %n 2 prec 30❙
  
  // all elements in Upto n are different❙
  lift_last_injective: {n,i} ⊦ lift i =ͭ last n ⟶ ↯❙
  lift_lift_injective: {n,i,j: tm Upto n} ⊦ lift i =ͭ lift j ⟶ ⊦ i =ͭ j❙

  // Upto zero is empty.❙
  induction_zero: {F: tm Upto zero ⟶ prop, i: tm Upto zero} ⊦ F i❙
  // Upto n' consists of n and the liftings of the elements of Upto n❙
  induction_succ: {n, F: tm Upto n' ⟶ prop} ({i: tm Upto n} ⊦ F (lift i)) ⟶ ⊦ F (last n) ⟶
                  {i: tm Upto n'} ⊦ F i❙
  
  // The following rules makes every natural number literal i a literal of type Upto n for a literal n with i<n.
  It does not introduce any kind of subtyping between Upto types or ℕ.❙
  rule ☞scala://numbers.latin2?UptoLiterals❙
  
  // embed Upto n into ℕ❙
  fulllift: {n} tm Upto n ⟶ ℕ❘# %n 2 prec 50❙
  fulllift_last: {n} ⊦ fulllift (last n) =ͭ n❘ role Simplify❙
  fulllift_lift: {n,i:tm Upto n} ⊦ fulllift (lift i) =ͭ fulllift i❘# role Simplify❙

theory NatUnary =
  include ?Numbers❙
  Nat = tm num❘# ℕ❙
❚

theory NatPeano =
  include ?NatUnary❙
  
  zero_succ_different : {n} ⊦ ¬(n' =ͭ zero)❙
  succ_injective : {m,n} ⊦ m' =ͭ n' ⟶ ⊦ m =ͭ n❙

  // the general case: the below could be derived from the following, which however requires polymorphic LF❙
  // induction : {T: ℕ ⟶ type} T zero ⟶ ({n} T n ⟶ T (n')) ⟶ {n}T n❙

  inductive_fun : {B, P: ℕ ⟶ tm B} tm B ⟶ (ℕ ⟶ tm B ⟶ tm B) ⟶ ℕ ⟶ tm B❙
  inductive_pred : {P: ℕ ⟶ prop} prop ⟶ (ℕ ⟶ prop ⟶ prop) ⟶ ℕ ⟶ prop❙
  inductive_proof : {P: ℕ ⟶ prop} ⊦ P zero ⟶ ({n} ⊦ P n ⟶ ⊦ P (n')) ⟶ {n} ⊦ P n❙
❚

theory NatPlus =
  include ?NatUnary❙
  include ?Plus❙
  
  plus_zero : {n} ⊦ n + zero =ͭ n❘role Simplify ❙  
  plus_zero_r : {n} ⊦ zero + n =ͭ n❘role Simplify ❙  
  plus_succ : {m, n} ⊦ n + m' =ͭ (n + m)'❘role Simplify❙              
  plus_succ_l : {m, n} ⊦ n' + m =ͭ (n + m)'❘role Simplify❙
  
  assoc_plus : {l,m,n} ⊦ (l+m)+n =ͭ l+(m+n) ❙  
  comm_plus : {m,n} ⊦ m+n =ͭ n+m ❙ 
❚


theory NatPlusTimes =
  include ?NatPlus❙
  include ?Times❙
  
  times_zero : {n} ⊦ zero * n =ͭ zero ❘role Simplify ❙
  times_zero_l : {n} ⊦ n * zero =ͭ zero ❘role Simplify ❙
  times_succ : {m,n} ⊦ n' * m =ͭ (n * m) + m❘role Simplify ❙
  times_succ_r : {m,n} ⊦ n * m' =ͭ (n * m) + n❘role Simplify ❙
  
  assoc_times: {l,m,n} ⊦ (l*m)*n =ͭ l*(m*n) ❙  
  comm_times : {m,n} ⊦ m*n =ͭ n*m ❙
❚

theory NatParity =
  include ?NatUnary❙
 
  even: ℕ ⟶ prop❘ # %n 1 prec 50❙
  odd: ℕ ⟶ prop❘ # %n 1 prec 50❙
  even_zero: ⊦ even zero❙
  even_succ: {n} ⊦ even n ⟶ ⊦ odd n'❙
  odd_zero: ⊦ ¬ odd zero❙
  odd_succ: {n} ⊦ odd n ⟶ ⊦ even n'❙
❚

theory NatAx =
  include ?NatPeano❙
  include ?NatPlusTimes❙
  include ?NatParity❙
❚

theory NatLiterals =
  include ?NatUnary❙

  rule rules?Realize (tm num) uom?StandardNat❙
  rule rules?Realize zero uom?Arithmetic/Zero❙
  rule rules?Realize succ uom?Arithmetic/Succ❙
❚

theory Nat =
  include ?NatPeano❙
  include ?NatPlusTimes❙
  include ?NatParity❙
  include ?NatLiterals❙
 
  lesser: tm num ⟶ tm num ⟶ prop❘# 1 < 2 prec 30❙ 
  lesser_zero_r: {n} ⊦ ¬(n < zero)❘role Simplify ❙ 
  lesser_zero_l: {n} ⊦ (zero <  n')❘role Simplify ❙ 
  lesser_succ: {x,y} ⊦ (x < y) ⇔  ( x' < y')❘role Simplify ❙ 

  greater: tm num ⟶ tm num⟶ prop ❘# 1 > 2 prec 30❘
  	= [x,y] y < x❙
  lesserequal: tm num ⟶ tm num ⟶ prop ❘# 1 %n 2 prec 30❘
    	= [x,y] ¬ (x < y) ❙
  greaterequal:  tm num ⟶ tm num ⟶ prop ❘# 1 ≥ 2 prec 30❘
  	= [x,y] ¬ (x < y ) ❙

  distributive: {l,m,n} ⊦ (l+m)*n =ͭ (l*n)+(m*n)❙

❚

namespace latin:/❚

fixmeta latin:/?HOLND❚

// Church numerals use a trick to define natural numbers as certain functions relative to an 
   arbitrary empty fixed type❚
theory ChurchNaturals =
  
  // an arbitrary type; note that there are no functions that return n, i.e., n is empty❙
  I: tp❙
  
  include ?SFOLEQND❙
  realize ?NatUnary❙

  // the following function type allows capturing exactly the natural numbers:
     The trick is that after binding [z:n,s:n⟶n], the only way to return something of type n is 
     to use z and s - that amounts to the usual construction of the natural numbers using zero and 
     successor.❙
     
  num = I → (I → I) → I❙

  // intuition: for [n: num], the term n a b is the result of applying function b n-times to a❙
  zero = λ[z]λ[s] z❙

  // succ : num ⟶ num = λn:I⟶(I ⟶ I)⟶I. λz:I. λs:I⟶I. s (n z s)❙ 
  succ = [n]λ[z]λ[s] s @ (n @ z @ s)❙
❚

theory ChurchNaturalsPlus =
  include ?ChurchNaturals❙
 
  realize ?NatPlus❙
  // intuition: m+n is the result of applying s m-times to n❙
  plus = [m,n]λ[z]λ[s] m @ (n @ z @ s) @ s❙
  
  plus_zero = _ ❙
  plus_succ = _ ❙
❚

theory ChurchNaturalsPlusTimes =
  include ?ChurchNaturalsPlus❙
  
  realize ?NatPlusTimes❙
  
  // intuition: m*n is the result of applying _+n m-times to z
     [u] n u s is the function that applies s n-times to u
     m z ([u] n u s) applies that function m-times to z
     this results in m*n applications of s to z❙
  times = [m,n]λ[z]λ[s] m @ z @ (λ[u] n @ u @ s)❙
  
  times_zero = _ ❙
  times_succ = _ ❙
❚
</content>

import rules scala://structuralfeatures.lf.mmt.kwarc.info❚

// Mainly ported (with very minor modifications)
// from Colin's examples/induction/NatExample.mmt
❚

theory NatInduct : http://cds.omdoc.org/examples?LFXI =
  inductive nat() ❘=
    n: type  ❙
    z: n     ❙
    s: n ⟶ n ❙
  ❚

  inductive_definition plusn() : nat() ❘=
    n: type  ❘= (nat/n ⟶ nat/n)     ❙
    z: n     ❘= ([x] x)             ❙
    s: n ⟶ n ❘= ([u,x] nat/s (u x)) ❙
  ❚

  plus: nat/n ⟶ nat/n ⟶ nat/n
    ❘= plusn/n
    ❘# 1 + 2
  ❙

  z_plus_n: {m: nat/n} DED ((nat/z + m) EQ m) ❙
  z_plus_z: DED (nat/z + nat/z) EQ nat/z ❙
  z_plus_suc: {m: nat/n} DED (nat/z + m) EQ m ⟶ DED (nat/z + (nat/s m)) EQ (nat/s m) ❙

  ind_proof z_neutral() : nat() ❘=
    n = [m] DED (nat/z + m) EQ m ❙
    z : n nat/z ❘= plusn/z/Applied nat/z ❙
    s : {x:nat/n} n x ⟶ n (nat/s x) ❘= [x, px] plusn/z/Applied (nat/s x) ❙
  ❚

  inductive_definition times() : nat() ❘=
    n: type  ❘= (nat/n ⟶ nat/n)     ❙
    z: n     ❘= ([x] nat/z)         ❙
    s: n ⟶ n ❘= ([u,x] (x + (u x))) ❙
  ❚
  mult: nat/n ⟶ nat/n ⟶ nat/n
    ❘= times/n
    ❘# 1 * 2
  ❙

  inductive_definition predec() : nat() ❘=
    n: type  ❘= nat/n   ❙
    z: n     ❘= nat/z   ❙
    s: n ⟶ n ❘= ([u] u) ❙
  ❚

  inductive_definition monus() : nat() ❘=
    n: type  ❘= (nat/n ⟶ nat/n)        ❙
    z: n     ❘= ([x] x)                ❙
    s: n ⟶ n ❘= ([u,x] predec/n (u x)) ❙
  ❚

import rules scala://lf.mmt.kwarc.info❚
import uom scala://uom.api.mmt.kwarc.info❚

theory IntUnary =
  include ?NatUnary❙
  
  pred: tm num ⟶ tm num ❘# p 1❙
  inv: tm num ⟶ tm num❘ # %n 1 prec 32❙

  pred_succ: {x} ⊦ (p x') =ͭ x ❘ role Simplify ❙
  succ_pred: {x} ⊦ (p x)'  =ͭ x ❘ role Simplify ❙
  
  inv_zero:  ⊦ inv zero =ͭ zero ❘ role Simplify ❙
  inv_succ: {x} ⊦ (inv  x' )  =ͭ  p inv x ❘ role Simplify ❙
  inv_pred: {x} ⊦ (inv p x)  =ͭ ( inv x)'  ❘ role Simplify ❙
  // axioms for succ and pred inverse❙
❚

theory IntPlus =
  include ?IntUnary❙
  include ?NatPlus❙
   plus_pred_l : {x,y} ⊦ (p x + y) =ͭ p(x + y) ❘ role Simplify ❙
   plus_pred_r : {x,y} ⊦ (x + p y) =ͭ p(x + y) ❘ role Simplify ❙
   plus_inv : {x,y} ⊦ inv (x + y) =ͭ (inv x) + (inv y) ❘ role Simplify ❙
  // axiom for + and pred❙
❚

theory IntPlusTimes =
  include ?IntUnary❙
  include ?NatPlusTimes❙
  

  times_pred_l : {x,y} ⊦ ( (p x) * y) =ͭ ((x*y)+ inv y) ❘ role Simplify ❙
  times_pred_r : {x,y} ⊦ ( x* (p y)) =ͭ ((x*y)+ inv x) ❘ role Simplify ❙
  
  times_inv : {x,y} ⊦ inv (x*y) =ͭ (inv x)*y❘ role Simplify ❙
  // axiom for * and pred❙
❚
theory IntSub =
	include ?IntPlusTimes ❙

	sub: tm num ⟶ tm num ⟶ tm num ❘ # 1 - 2 prec 31❙ 
	
	sub_zero_r : {x} ⊦ (x - zero) =ͭ  x ❘role Simplify❙
  sub_zero_l: {y} ⊦ (zero - y) =ͭ  inv y ❘role Simplify❙ 
  
  sub_succ_l : {x,y} ⊦ x' - y =ͭ ( x - y )'❘role Simplify❙
  sub_succ_r : {x,y} ⊦ x - (y') =ͭ p( x - y )❘role Simplify❙

  neutRight: {a,x:tm &a} ⊦ x∘neutral =ͭ x❙
❚

theory EndoIdempotent =
  include ?EndoMagma❙
  idempotent: {a,x:tm &a} ⊦ x∘x =ͭ x❙
❚

theory EndoFirstNonNeutral =
  include ?EndoNeutral❙
  firstNonNeutral: {a,x,y:tm &a} (⊦ x =ͭ neutral ⟶ ↯) ⟶ ⊦ x∘y =ͭ x❙

theory EndoMonoid =
  include ?EndoSemigroup❙

theory EndoCommSemigroup =

  include ?EndoCommutative❙

theory EndoBand =

  include ?EndoIdempotent❙

theory EndoCommMonoid =

  include ?EndoCommSemigroup❙

namespace latin:/❚

fixmeta ?HOLND❚

ref ?CategoryOfTypes❚

theory Applicative =
  include ?TypeOperator❙
  pure : {a} tm a ⟶ tm &a❘# pure 2 prec 60❙
  splat: {a,b} tm &(a→b) ⟶ tm &a ⟶ tm &b❘# 3 <*> 4 prec 50❙
  
  identity: {a,X:tm &a} ⊦ pure (ident a) <*> X =ͭ X❙
  homomorphism: {a,b,f:tm a→b,x} ⊦ pure f <*> pure x =ͭ pure (f@x)❙
  interchange: {a,b,F:tm &(a→b), x} ⊦ F <*> pure x =ͭ pure (applyTo x) <*> F❙
  composition: {a,b,c,F:tm &(a→b),G:tm &(b→c),X} ⊦ G <*> (F <*> X) =ͭ pure (λ[f]λ[g]f;g) <*> F <*> G <*> X❙
  
  // The remaining implementation is missing ❙
  // realize ?InternalEndoFunctor❙
  // fmap = [a,b,f] λ[X] pure f <*> X❙
❚

theory Monad =
  include ?TypeOperator❙
  Return : {a} tm a ⟶ tm &a❘# Return 2 prec 60❙
  Bind : {a,b} tm &a ⟶ (tm a ⟶ tm &b) ⟶ tm &b❘# 3 >>= 4 prec 50❙
  
  identLeft: {a,b,f:tm a ⟶ tm &b,x} ⊦ Return x >>= f =ͭ f x❙
  identRight: {a,X: tm &a} ⊦ X >>= ([x] Return x) =ͭ X❙
  assoc : {a,b,c,f:tm a ⟶ tm &b, g:tm b ⟶ tm &c,X} ⊦ (X >>= f) >>= g =ͭ X >>= [x] ((f x) >>= g)❙
  
  // The remaining implementation is missing ❙
  // realize ?EndoFunctor❙
  // applyFun = [a,b,f,X] X >>= [x] Return (f x)❙
❚

theory InternalMonad =
  include ?TypeOperator❙
  return : {a} tm a→&a❙
  bind : {a,b} tm &a→(a→&b)→&b❙

  structure laws : ?Monad =
    include ?TypeOperator❙
    Return = [a,x] (return a) @ x❘# Return 2 prec 60❙
    Bind = [a,b,X,F] (bind a b) @ X @ (λ F)❘# 3 >>= 4 prec 50❙
  ❚

  // The remaining implementation is missing ❙
  // realize ?Applicative❙
  // pure = [a,x] Return x❙
  // splat = [a,b,F,X] F >>= [f] X >>= [x] Return (f@x)❙
❚

view KleisliCat : ?Category → ?InternalMonad =
  obj = tp❙
  hom = [a,b] a→&b❙
  ident = [a] return a❙
  // comp = [a,b,c,f,g] λ[x] Return x >>= ([x]f@x) >>= ([y]g@y)❘# 4 >=> 5 prec 50❙
  // assignments to neutrality and associativity axioms missing❙
❚

<content>
namespace latin:/❚

fixmeta ?BigSFOL❚

theory Collection =
  include ?EndoMagma❙
  include ?EndoNeutral❙
  include ?Nat❙
  
  empty: {a} tm &a❘ # %n 1❘= [a] neutral❙

  singleton : {a} tm a ⟶ tm &a❘# %n 2 prec 100❙
  cons : {a} tm a ⟶ tm &a ⟶ tm &a❘# %n 2 3 prec 60❘= [a,x,xs] singleton x ∘ xs❙

  inductive_proof: {a,P: tm &a ⟶ prop} ⊦ P neutral ⟶ ({x,xs} ⊦ P xs ⟶ ⊦ P (cons x xs)) ⟶ {xs} ⊦ P xs ❙

  is_empty : {a} tm &a ⟶ prop❘# %n 2 prec 40❙
  is_empty_neutral: {a} ⊦ is_empty (empty a)❙
  is_empty_cons : {a,x,xs: tm & a} ⊦ ¬is_empty (cons x xs)❙
  is_empty_singleton : {a,x: tm a} ⊦ ¬is_empty (singleton x)❙
  is_empty_concat : {a,l, m: tm &a} ⊦ is_empty l ⟶ ⊦ is_empty m ⟶ ⊦ is_empty l∘m❙

  is_nonempty : {a} tm &a ⟶ prop❘# %n 2 prec 50❘	= [a,xs] ¬(is_empty xs)❙ 	         

  size: {a} tm &a ⟶ ℕ❘# %n 2 prec 40❙
  size_neutral : {a} ⊦ size (empty a) =ͭ zero ❙
	size_singleton : {a,x: tm a} ⊦ size (singleton x) =ͭ one❙
	
	contain : {a} tm & a ⟶ tm a ⟶ prop❘# %n 2 3 prec 50❙
	contain_neutral: {a,x: tm a} ⊦ ¬ contain (empty a) x❙
	contain_cons1 : {a,x:tm a,xs} ⊦  contain (cons x xs) x ❙
	contain_cons2 : {a,x,y,ys: tm & a} ⊦ ¬ x=ͭy ⟶ ⊦ contain (cons y ys) x ⇔ contain ys x❙

	count: {a} tm a ⟶ tm &a ⟶ ℕ❘# %n 2 3 prec 30❙
	count_neutral : {a:tp,x:tm a} ⊦ count x (empty a) =ͭ zero❙
	count_singleton : {a,x:tm a} ⊦ count x (singleton x) =ͭ one❙
	
	remove: {a} tm a ⟶ tm &a ⟶ tm &a ❘# %n 2 3 prec 50❙
	remove_neutral : {a:tp,u:tm a} ⊦ remove u neutral =ͭ neutral❙
	remove_cons1 : {a,x:tm a,xs} ⊦ remove x (cons x xs) =ͭ xs ❙
	remove_cons2 : {a,u: tm a,x,xs} ⊦ ¬ (u =ͭ x) ⟶ ⊦ remove u (cons x xs) =ͭ cons x (remove u xs)❙
	
	removeAll: {a} tm a ⟶ tm &a ⟶ tm &a❘ # %n 2 3 prec 50❙
	removeAll_neutral : {a:tp,u:tm a} ⊦ removeAll u neutral =ͭ neutral❙
	removeAll_cons1 : {a,x:tm a,xs} ⊦ removeAll x (cons x xs) =ͭ removeAll x xs ❙
	removeAll_cons2 : {a,u: tm a,x,xs} ⊦ ¬ (u =ͭ x) ⟶ ⊦ removeAll u (cons x xs) =ͭ cons x (removeAll u xs)❙

  filter : {a} (tm a ⟶ prop) ⟶ tm &a ⟶ tm &a❘# %n 2 3 prec 50❙
  filter_neutral : {a,f: tm a ⟶ prop} 
  						⊦ filter f neutral =ͭ neutral❙
  filter_cons1 : {a, f: tm a ⟶ prop,x,xs} 
  						⊦   f x  ⟶ ⊦ filter f (cons x xs) =ͭ cons x (filter f xs)❙
  filter_cons2 : {a, f: tm a ⟶ prop,x,xs} 
  						⊦ ¬(f x) ⟶ ⊦ filter f (cons x xs) =ͭ filter f xs❙
  filter_singleton1 : {a,f: tm a ⟶ prop,x} 
  						⊦   f x  ⟶ ⊦ filter f (singleton x) =ͭ singleton x❙
  filter_singleton2 : {a,f: tm a ⟶ prop,x} 
  						⊦ ¬(f x) ⟶ ⊦ filter f (singleton x) =ͭ neutral❙
  filter_op: {a,f: tm a ⟶ prop,l, m}
  						⊦ filter f (l∘m) =ͭ (filter f l) ∘ (filter f m)❙

  	map : {a,b} (tm a ⟶ tm b) ⟶ tm &a ⟶ tm &b❘# %n 3 4 prec 50❙
  map_neutral : {a,b,f: tm a ⟶ tm b} ⊦ map f neutral =ͭ neutral ❙
  map_cons : {a,b, f: tm a ⟶ tm b,x,xs} ⊦ map f (cons x xs) =ͭ cons (f x) (map f xs)❙
  map_singleton : {a,b,f: tm a ⟶ tm b,x} ⊦ map f (singleton x) =ͭ singleton (f x)❙
  map_op: {a,b,f: tm a ⟶ tm b,l, m} ⊦ map f (l∘m) =ͭ (map f l)∘(map f m)❙

  	flatmap : {a,b} (tm a ⟶ tm &b) ⟶ tm &a ⟶ tm &b❘# %n 3 4 prec 50❙
  flatmap_neutral : {a,b,f: tm a ⟶ tm &b} ⊦ flatmap f neutral =ͭ neutral ❙
  flatmap_cons : {a,b, f: tm a ⟶ tm &b,x,xs: tm &a} 
  						⊦ flatmap f (cons x xs) =ͭ (f x) ∘ (flatmap f xs)❙
  flatmap_singleton : {a,b,f: tm a ⟶ tm &b,x: tm a} 
  						⊦ flatmap f (singleton x) =ͭ f x❙
  flatmap_op: {a,b,f: tm a ⟶ tm &b,l, m: tm &a}
  						⊦ flatmap f (l∘m) =ͭ (flatmap f l) ∘ (flatmap f m)❙

  exists : {a} (tm a ⟶ prop) ⟶ tm &a ⟶ prop❘# %n 2 3 prec 30❙
  exists_empty : {a, f: tm a ⟶ prop} ⊦ ¬ exists f (empty a)❙
  exists_cons1 : {a, f: tm a ⟶ prop,x,xs} ⊦ exists f (cons x xs) ⇔ f x ∨ (exists f xs)❙
  exists_singleton : {a,f: tm a ⟶ prop,x} ⊦ exists f (singleton x) ⇔ f x❙
  exists_op: {a,f: tm a ⟶ prop,l, m} ⊦ exists f (l∘m) ⇔ (exists f l ∨ exists f m)❙

  forall : {a} (tm a ⟶ prop) ⟶ tm &a ⟶ prop❘# %n 2 3 prec 30❙
  forall_empty : {a, f: tm a ⟶ prop} ⊦ forall f (empty a)❙
  forall_cons1 : {a, f: tm a ⟶ prop,x,xs} ⊦ forall f (cons x xs) ⇔ f x ∧ (forall f xs)❙
  forall_singleton : {a,f: tm a ⟶ prop,x} ⊦ forall f (singleton x) ⇔ f x❙
  forall_op: {a,f: tm a ⟶ prop,l, m} ⊦ forall f (l∘m) ⇔ (forall f l ∧ forall f m)❙
❚

theory NonIdempotentCollection =
  include ?Collection❙
	size_cons : {a,x,xs: tm &a} ⊦ size (cons x xs) =ͭ (size xs)'❙
	size_op : {a,l, m: tm &a} ⊦ size (l∘m) =ͭ (size l) + (size m)❙

	count_cons1 : {a,x:tm a,xs} ⊦ count x (cons x xs) =ͭ (count x xs)'❙
	count_cons2 : {a,y:tm a,x:tm a,xs} ⊦ ¬ y =ͭ x ⟶ ⊦ count y (cons x xs) =ͭ count x xs❙
  count_op : {a,x:tm a,xs,ys} ⊦ count x (xs∘ys) =ͭ (count x xs)+(count x ys)❙
❚

theory CommutativeCollection =
	include ?Collection❙		

❚

theory BinaryTreeSpec =
	include ?Collection ❙
❚

theory ListSpec =
  include ?NonIdempotentCollection❙
  include ?EndoMonoid❙
❚


theory MultisetSpec =
  include ?ListSpec❙
  include ?EndoCommutative❙

  	intersect: {a} tm &a ⟶ tm &a ⟶ tm &a❘# %n 2 3 prec 30❙ 
	intersect_neutral1 : {a, xs: tm &a} ⊦ intersect neutral xs =ͭ neutral❙
	intersect_neutral2 : {a, xs: tm &a} ⊦ intersect xs neutral =ͭ neutral❙
	intersect_cons1: {a,x: tm a, xs,ys: tm &a} 
									⊦ (contain ys x) ⟶ ⊦ intersect (cons x xs) ys 
										=ͭ cons x (intersect xs (remove x ys))❙
	intersect_cons2: {a,x: tm a, xs,ys: tm &a} 
									⊦ ¬ (contain ys x) ⟶ ⊦ intersect (cons x xs) ys 
										=ͭ intersect xs ys ❙
❚


theory FiniteSetSpec =
  include ?MultisetSpec❙
  include ?EndoIdempotent❙
❚

theory OptionSpec =
  include ?ListSpec❙
  include ?EndoFirstNonNeutral❙
❚


theory ResultSpec =
	include ?Collection❙
  include ?EndoMonoid❙
  
❚

theory Lists =
	include ?Nat❙
  structure list : ?ListSpec =
  	  include ?Nat❙
    applyType # List 1❙
    op # 2 concat 3 prec 50❙
    neutral # nil %I1❙
 ❚ 	
❚

theory Multisets =
	include ?Nat❙
  structure multiset : ?MultisetSpec =
  	  include ?Nat❙
    applyType # Multiset 1❙
    op # 2 munion 3❙
    neutral # mempty %I1❙ 
    singleton # multiset 2❙
 ❚
❚

theory FiniteSets =
	include ?Nat❙
  structure finset : ?FiniteSetSpec =
    	include ?Nat❙
    applyType # FinSet 1❙
    op # 2 union 3❙
    neutral # empty %I1❙ 
    singleton # finset 2❙
 ❚
❚

theory BinaryTrees =
	structure binarytree : ?BinaryTreeSpec =
		applyType # BinaryTree 1❙
    op # 2 union 3❙
    neutral # none %I1❙ 
    singleton # leaf 2❙
    cons # node 2 3 ❙
	❚
❚

theory Options =
  structure option : ?OptionSpec =
    applyType # Option 1❙
    op # 2 orelse 3❙
    neutral # none %I1❙ 
    singleton # option 2❙
 ❚
❚

<content>
namespace latin:/❚

fixmeta ?BigSFOL❚

theory ListOperations =
	include ?Lists❙ 
	
	hd : {a} tm List a ⟶ tm a❘# %n 2 prec 40❙
 	hd_cons : {a,x: tm a,xs: tm List a} ⊦ hd (list/cons x xs) =ͭ  x❙
 	hd_singleton : {a,x: tm a} ⊦ hd list/singleton x =ͭ  x❙
 	hd_concat: {a,l, m: tm List a} ⊦ list/is_nonempty l ⟶ ⊦ hd (l concat m) =ͭ hd l❙
 
 	tl: {a} tm List a ⟶ tm List a❘# %n 2 prec 40❙
 	tl_cons : {a,x,xs: tm List a} ⊦ tl (list/cons x xs) =ͭ xs❙
 	tl_singleton : {a,x: tm a} ⊦ tl list/singleton x =ͭ nil❙
  tl_concat: {a,l, m: tm List a} ⊦ list/is_nonempty l ⟶ ⊦ tl (l concat m) =ͭ ((tl l) concat  m)❙
 
  snoc: {a} tm List a ⟶ tm a ⟶ tm List a❘# %n 2 3 prec 50❙
  snoc_nil : {a,x: tm a} ⊦ snoc nil x =ͭ list/singleton x❙
  snoc_cons : {a, y,x,xs: tm List a} ⊦ snoc (list/cons x xs) x =ͭ list/cons x (snoc xs y)❙
  snoc_singleton : {a,y,x: tm a} ⊦ snoc (list/singleton x) y =ͭ list/cons x (list/singleton y)❙
  snoc_op : {a,y,l, m: tm List a} ⊦ snoc (l concat m) y =ͭ l concat (snoc m y)❙

	rev: {a} tm List a ⟶ tm List a❘# %n 2 prec 30❙
	rev_nil: {a} ⊦ rev (list/empty a) =ͭ nil❙
  rev_cons: {a,x,xs: tm List a} ⊦ rev (list/cons x xs) =ͭ snoc (rev xs) x❙ 
  rev_singleton : {a,x: tm a} ⊦ rev (list/singleton x) =ͭ list/singleton x❙
  rev_concat: {a,l, m: tm List a} ⊦ rev (l concat m) =ͭ (rev m) concat (rev l)❙

  drop: {a} tm List a ⟶ ℕ ⟶ tm List a❘# %n 2 3 prec 50❙ 
  drop_zero : {a,xs: tm List a} ⊦ drop xs zero =ͭ xs❙
  drop_succ: {a,n,x,xs: tm List a} ⊦ drop (list/cons x xs) (n') =ͭ drop xs n❙
  drop_nil : {a,n} ⊦ drop (nil: tm List a) n =ͭ nil ❙
  drop_singleton : {a,n,x: tm a} ⊦ drop (list/singleton x) n =ͭ nil❙
 
  list_match : {a,b} tm List a ⟶ tm b ⟶ (tm a ⟶ tm List a ⟶ tm b) ⟶ tm b❘
             # 3 match_list case_nil 4 case_cons 5  prec 50❙
  list_match_nil: {a,b,nilcase,conscase:tm a ⟶ tm List a ⟶ tm b}  
  							⊦ nil match_list case_nil nilcase case_cons conscase =ͭ nilcase❙
  list_match_cons: {a,b,nilcase: tm b,conscase,x,xs:tm List a} 
  							⊦ (list/cons x xs) match_list case_nil nilcase case_cons conscase =ͭ conscase x xs ❙

  	foldl : {a,b} (tm b ⟶ tm a ⟶ tm b) ⟶ tm b ⟶ tm List a ⟶ tm b❘# %n 3 4 5 prec 50❙
  foldl_nil : {a,b,f: tm b ⟶ tm a ⟶ tm b,y}
            ⊦ foldl f y nil =ͭ y ❙
  foldl_cons : {a,b,f: tm b ⟶ tm a ⟶ tm b,y,x,xs} 
  						⊦ foldl f y (list/cons x xs) =ͭ foldl f (f y x) xs ❙
  foldl_singleton : {a,b,f: tm b ⟶ tm a ⟶ tm b,y,x} 
  						⊦ foldl f y (list/singleton x) =ͭ f y x❙
  foldl_concat: {a,b,f: tm b ⟶ tm a ⟶ tm b,y,l, m} 
  						⊦ foldl f y (l concat m) =ͭ foldl f (foldl f y l) m❙

  foldr : {a,b} (tm a ⟶ tm b ⟶ tm b) ⟶ tm b ⟶ tm List a ⟶ tm b❘# %n 3 4 5 prec 50❙
  foldr_nil : {a,b,f: tm a ⟶ tm b ⟶ tm b,y} 
  						⊦ foldr f y nil =ͭ y ❙
  foldr_cons : {a,b,f: tm a ⟶ tm b ⟶ tm b,y,x,xs} 
  						⊦ foldr f y (list/cons x xs) =ͭ f x (foldr f y xs) ❙
  foldr_singleton : {a,b,f: tm a ⟶ tm b ⟶ tm b,y,x} 
  						⊦ foldr f y (list/singleton x) =ͭ f x y❙
  foldr_concat: {a,b,f: tm a ⟶ tm b ⟶ tm b,y: tm b,l,m} 
  						⊦foldr f y (l concat m) =ͭ foldr f (foldr f y m) l❙
❚

theory ListZip =
	include ?ListOperations❙  
	include ?SimpleProducts❙
  
  zip : {a,b} tm List a ⟶ tm List b ⟶ tm List a ×ͭ b❘# %n 3 4 prec 50❙
  zip_neutral : {a,b} 
  						⊦ zip (nil: tm List a) (nil: tm List b) =ͭ nil❙
  zip_cons : {a,b,x:tm a,xs,y:tm b,ys} 
  						⊦ zip (list/cons x xs) (list/cons y ys) =ͭ list/cons (x,ͭy) (zip xs ys)❙
  zip_singleton: {a,b,x:tm a,y: tm b} 
  						⊦ zip (list/singleton x) (list/singleton y) =ͭ list/singleton (x,ͭy)❙
  zip_concat: {a,b,l1,m1: tm List a,l2,m2: tm List b} 
  						⊦ zip (l1 concat m1) (l2 concat m2) =ͭ (zip l1 l2) concat (zip m1 m2)❙
  						  
  unzip : {a,b} tm List (a ×ͭ b) ⟶ tm (List a)×ͭ(List b)❘# %n 3 prec 50❙
  unzip_nil : {a,b} 
  						⊦ unzip (nil: tm List (a×ͭb)) =ͭ (nil,ͭnil)❙
  unzip_cons : {a,b,x: tm a, y : tm b, xys: tm List a ×ͭ b}

module modules {
    theory Scalars {
        scalars: .relations.Carrier
    }

    theory RingScalars {
        include Scalars
        scalars: .ringoids.Ring
    }

    theory SkewFieldScalars {
        include Scalars
        scalars: .ringoids.SkewField 

    }

    theory FieldScalars {
        include Scalars
        scalars: .ringoids.Field 
    }

    theory LeftModule {
        include Scalars
        include .groups.CommGroup
        left_scalars: RingScalars

        left_scalar_mult: (scalars.univ, univ) -> univ # infix ⋅
        left_identity:--- (left_scalars.scalars.mult.e) ⋅ x == x
        left_distrib_scalars:--- (left_scalars.scalars.add.op(s1,s2)) ⋅ x == (s1 ⋅ x) ∘ (s2 ⋅ x)
        left_distrib_vectors:--- s ⋅ (x ∘ y) == (s ⋅ x) ∘ (s ⋅ y) 
        left_assoc:--- left_scalars.scalars.mult.op(s1, s2) ⋅ x == s1 ⋅ (s2 ⋅ x) 
    }

    theory RightModule {
        include RingScalars
        include .groups.CommGroup
        right_scalars: RingScalars

        right_scalar_mult: (univ, scalars.univ) -> univ # infix ⋅
        right_identity:--- x ⋅ (right_scalars.scalars.mult.e) == x
        right_distrib_scalars:--- x ⋅ (right_scalars.scalars.add.op(s1,s2)) == (x ⋅ s1) ∘ (x ⋅ s2)
        right_distrib_vectors:--- (x ∘ y) ⋅ s == (x ⋅ s) ∘ (y ⋅ s)
        right_assoc:--- x ⋅ right_scalars.scalars.mult.op(s1, s2) == (x ⋅ s1) ⋅ s2
    }

    theory BiModule {
        include LeftModule
        include RightModule
    }

    theory LeftVectorSpace {
        include LeftModule
        left_scalars: SkewFieldScalars
    }

    theory RightVectorSpace {
        include RightModule
        right_scalars: SkewFieldScalars
    }

    theory VectorSpace {
        include LeftModule
        left_scalars: FieldScalars
    }
}

module monoids {
    theory UnitElement {
        include .magmas.Magma
        e : univ
        realize .magmas.Pointed
        point = e
        involution : univ -> bool = x -> (x∘x == e)
    }

    theory RightUnital {
        include UnitElement
        neutralR:--- x∘e == x
    }

    theory LeftUnital {
        include UnitElement
        neutralL:--- e∘x == x
    }

    theory Unital {
        include LeftUnital
        include RightUnital
    }

    theory FirstNonNeutral {
        include Unital
        FirstNonNeutral:--- x != e => forall y. x∘y == x
    }

    theory LastNonNeutral {
        include Unital
        LastNonNeutral:--- y != e => forall x. x∘y == y
    }

    theory Powers {
        include .magmas.PowerAssociative
        include Unital
        include .Numbers.Nat
        power: (univ, num) -> univ
        power_zero:--- power(x, .Numbers.Nat.z) == e
        power_succ:--- power(x, .Numbers.Nat.s(n)) == power(x, n) ∘ x
    }

    theory Monoid {
        include .magmas.Semigroup
        include Unital
        inverse: (univ, univ) -> bool = (x, y) -> (x∘y == e) & (y∘x == e)
        inverse_sym:--- inverse(x, y) => inverse(y, x)
        inverse_unique:--- inverse(x, y1) & inverse(x, y2) => (y1 == y2)
        inverse_neutral:--- inverse(e, e)
        inverse_op:--- inverse(x1, x2) & inverse(y1, y2) => inverse(x1∘y1, x2∘y2) 
        involution_inverse:--- (involution(x) => inverse(x, x)) & (inverse(x, x) => involution(x))
    }

    theory Involutory {
        include Monoid
        involutory:--- involution(x)
        inverse_refl:--- inverse(x,x)
        inverse_ident:--- inverse(x,y) => (x == y)
    }

    theory IdempotentMonoid {
        include Monoid
        include .magmas.Band
    }

    theory CommMonoid {
        include Monoid
        include .magmas.CommSemigroup
    }

    theory BoundedSemilattice {
        include .magmas.Semilattice
        include CommMonoid
    }
}

namespace latin:/algebraic❚

fixmeta latin:/?SFOLEQND❚

theory Relation =
  include ?Set❙
  rel : U ⟶ U ⟶ prop❘# 1 $ 2 prec 30❙
  
  total structure metarel : latin:/?Relation =
    carrier = U❙
    rel = [x,y] ⊦ x $ y❙
  ❚
   
  isSmallest: U ⟶ (U ⟶ prop) ⟶ prop❘ = [x,p] p x ∧ ∀ͭ[z] p z ⇒ x$z❘# 1 isSmallest 2❙
  isGreatest: U ⟶ (U ⟶ prop) ⟶ prop❘ = [x,p] p x ∧ ∀ͭ[z] p z ⇒ z$x❘# 1 isGreatest 2❙

  below2 = [x,y,u] u$x ∧ u$y❙
  above2 = [x,y,u] x$u ∧ y$u❙

  infimumOf = [x,y,i] i isGreatest below2 x y❙
  infimumI : {x,y,i} ⊦i$x ⟶ ⊦i$y ⟶ ({z} ⊦z$x ⟶ ⊦z$y ⟶ ⊦z$i) ⟶ ⊦ infimumOf x y i❘
           = [x,y,i,p,q,R] andI (andI p q) tforallI [z] implI [s] R z (s andEl) (s andEr)❙
  infimumE : {x,y,i,z} ⊦ infimumOf x y i ⟶ ⊦z$x ⟶ ⊦z$y ⟶ ⊦z$i❘
           = [x,y,i,z,p,q,r] p andEr tforallE z implE (andI q r)❙
 
  supremumOf = [x,y,s] s isSmallest above2 x y❙
  supremumI : {x,y,s} ⊦x$s ⟶ ⊦y$s ⟶ ({z} ⊦x$z ⟶ ⊦y$z ⟶ ⊦s$z) ⟶ ⊦ supremumOf x y s❘
           = [x,y,i,p,q,R] andI (andI p q) tforallI [z] implI [t] R z (t andEl) (t andEr)❙
  supremumE : {x,y,s,z} ⊦ supremumOf x y s ⟶ ⊦x$z ⟶ ⊦y$z ⟶ ⊦s$z❘
           = [x,y,s,z,p,q,r] p andEr tforallE z implE (andI q r)❙ 
❚

theory Reflexivity =
  include ?Relation❙
  refl : {x} ⊦ x$x❘# %n %I1❙
❚

theory Symmetry =
  include ?Relation❙
  sym : {x,y} ⊦ x$y ⟶ ⊦ y$x❘# 3 %n❙
❚

theory Transitivity =
  include ?Relation❙
  trans    : {x,y,z} ⊦ x$y ⟶ ⊦ y$z ⟶ ⊦ x$z❘# 4 %n 5❙
❚

theory Preorder =
  include ?Reflexivity❙
  include ?Transitivity❙
❚

theory EquivalenceRelation =
  include ?Preorder❙
  include ?Symmetry❙
❚

theory AntiSymmetry =
  include ?Relation❙
  antisym : {x,y} ⊦ x$y ⟶ ⊦ y$x ⟶ ⊦ x =ͭ y❘# %n 3 4❙
❚

</content>

<content>
namespace latin:/❚

fixmeta latin:/powertypes?PowerSFOL❚

theory BaseSet =
  include algebraic?Set❙
  X = universe❙
❚

// isomorphic axiomatizations of closure systems/operators❚
theory ClosureSystem =
  include ?BaseSet❙  
  CC : tm ℘ͯ℘ͯX❙
  
  intersection_closed : {Q: tm ℘ͯ℘ͯX} ⊦ Q ⊆ͯ CC ⟶ ⊦ ⋂ͯ Q ∈ͯ CC❙
  full_closed  : ⊦ fullset ∈ͯ CC❘
  				= biginter_empty tcongP ([A] A ∈ͯ CC) intersection_closed subset_empty❙
❚

theory ClosureOperator =
  include ?BaseSet❙  
  closure : tm ℘ͯX ⟶ tm ℘ͯX❘ # cl 1 prec 50❙
  
  extensive_closure    : {A} ⊦ A ⊆ͯ cl A❙
  monotone_closure     : {A,B} ⊦ A ⊆ͯ B ⟶ ⊦ cl A ⊆ͯ cl B❙
  idempotent_closure   : {A} ⊦ cl cl A =ͭ cl A❙
  
  closureFixI : {A} ⊦ cl A ⊆ͯ A ⟶ ⊦ cl A =ͭ A❘ 
  				= [A,p] subset_antisym p extensive_closure❙     
❚

theory Closeness =
  include ?BaseSet❙  
  close : tm X ⟶ tm ℘ͯX ⟶ prop❘ # 1 ⋶ 2 prec 40❙

  in_close          : {x,A} ⊦ x ∈ͯ A ⟶ ⊦ x ⋶ A❙
  bigger_close      : {x,A,B} ⊦ x ⋶ A ⟶ ⊦ A ⊆ͯ B ⟶ ⊦ x ⋶ B❙
  transitive_close  : {A,B,x} ⊦ x ⋶ B ⟶ ⊦ (∀ͭ [y] y ∈ͯ B ⇒ y ⋶ A) ⟶ ⊦ x ⋶ A❙
❚

// isomorphic axiomatizations of topologies❚

theory InteriorTopology = 
  include ?BaseSet❙  
  interior : tm ℘ͯX ⟶ tm ℘ͯX❘# interior 1 prec 50 ❙

  extensive_interior    : {A} ⊦ interior A ⊆ͯ A❙
  idempotent_interior   : {A} ⊦ interior A =ͭ interior interior A❙
  bin_inters_interior   : {A, B} ⊦ interior (A ∩ͯ B) =ͭ interior A ∩ͯ interior B❙
  preservation_interior : ⊦ interior full X =ͭ full X❙
  monotone_interior     : {A,B} ⊦ A ⊆ͯ B ⟶ ⊦ interior A ⊆ͯ interior B❘
								= [A,B,p] subset_trans
								(subset_trans (subset_eq_left (inter_subset_left p tcongT interior)) 
						                       subset_eq_left bin_inters_interior)
						         subset_inter_right❙
❚

theory ClosureTopology =
  include ?ClosureOperator❙

  empty_closure    : ⊦ cl empty X =ͭ empty X❙
  union_closure    : {A,B} ⊦ cl (A ∪ͯ B) =ͭ cl A ∪ͯ cl B❙
  
  // monotone_closure provable from union_closure❚
❚

theory ClosenessTopology =
  include ?Closeness❙

  empty_union_close  : {x} ⊦ ¬ x ⋶ empty X❙
  finite_union_close : {x,A,B} ⊦ x ⋶ (A ∪ͯ B) ⟶ ⊦ x ⋶ A ∨ x ⋶ B❙

  // bigger_close provable from union ❙
❚

theory OpenTopology =
  include ?BaseSet❙  
  OO    : tm ℘ͯ℘ͯX❙
  
  full_open  : ⊦ full X ∈ͯ OO❙
  union_open : {Q: tm ℘ͯ℘ͯX} ⊦ Q ⊆ͯ OO ⟶ ⊦ ⋃ͯ Q ∈ͯ OO❙
  finite_intersection_open : {A,B} ⊦ A ∈ͯ OO ⟶ ⊦ B ∈ͯ OO ⟶ ⊦ A ∩ͯ B ∈ͯ OO❙

  empty_open : ⊦ empty X ∈ͯ OO❘
   			    = bigunion_empty tcongP ([A] A ∈ͯ OO) union_open subset_empty❙
❚

// axioms/theorems are dual to OpenTopology❚
theory ClosedTopology =
  include ?ClosureSystem❙  
  empty_closed : ⊦ empty X ∈ͯ CC❙
  finite_union_closed : {A,B} ⊦ A ∈ͯ CC ⟶ ⊦ B ∈ͯ CC ⟶ ⊦ A ∪ͯ B ∈ͯ CC❙
❚

theory NeighborhoodTopology =
  include ?BaseSet❙  
  NN    : tm X ⟶ tm ℘ͯ℘ͯX❙
  neighborhood: tm X ⟶ tm ℘ͯX ⟶ prop❘
              = [x,N] N ∈ͯ NN x❘# 1 ∶ 2 prec 30❙
  
  nonempty_neighborhood : {x} ⊦ ¬ NN x =ͭ ∅ͯ❙
  in_neighborhood : {x: tm X,N} ⊦ x ∶ N ⟶ ⊦ x ∈ͯ N❙
  superset_closed_neighborhood : {M,N,x} ⊦ x ∶ M ⟶ ⊦ M ⊆ͯ N ⟶ ⊦ x ∶ N❙
  intersection_closed_neighborhood : {M,N,x} ⊦ x ∶ M ⟶ ⊦ x ∶ N ⟶ ⊦ x ∶ M ∩ͯ N❙
  openness_neighborhood : {N,x} ⊦ x ∶ N ⟶ ⊦ ∃ͭ[M]∀ͭ[y] x ∶ M ∧ (y∈ͯM ⇒ y ∶ N)❙
  fullset_neighborhood : {x} ⊦ x ∶ full X❘
           = [x] notemptyE 
             nonempty_neighborhood [N,p] superset_closed_neighborhood p subset_full❙
❚
</content>

namespace latin:/❚

fixmeta latin:/powertypes?PowerSFOL❚

theory TopologyMap =
  structure dom : ?Topology❙
  structure cod : ?Topology❙
  homX : tm dom/X ⟶ tm cod/X❙
❚

theory ReflectsClosedness =
  include ?TopologyMap❙
  reflectsClosedness : ⊦ ∀ͭ[C] C ∈ͯ cod/CC ⇒ C preimage homX ∈ͯ dom/CC❙
❚

theory ReflectsOpenness =
  include ?TopologyMap❙
  reflectsOpenness : ⊦ ∀ͭ[C] C ∈ͯ cod/OO ⇒ C preimage homX ∈ͯ dom/OO❙
❚

theory ReflectsNeighborhood =
  include ?TopologyMap❙
  reflectsNeighborhood : ⊦ ∀ͭ[d]∀ͭ[C] homX d cod/∶ C ⇒ d dom/∶ C preimage homX❙
❚

theory PreimageExpandsInterior =
  include ?TopologyMap❙
  preimageExpandsInterior : ⊦ ∀ͭ[C] (cod/interior C) preimage homX ⊆ͯ dom/interior (C preimage homX)❙
❚

theory ExpandsClosure =
  include ?TopologyMap❙
  expandsClosure : ⊦ ∀ͭ[D] (dom/cl D) map homX ⊆ͯ cod/cl (D map homX)❙
❚

theory PreservesCloseness =
  include ?TopologyMap❙
  preservesCloseness : ⊦ ∀ͭ[D]∀ͭ[d] d dom/⋶ D ⇒ (homX d) cod/⋶ (D map homX)❙
❚

view ReflectsOpennessToReflectsClosedness : ?ReflectsOpenness → ?ReflectsClosedness =
  include ?TopologyMap❙
  reflectsOpenness = tforallI [C] implI [p] pfilterI 
  					 (compl_preimage tcongP ([A] A ∈ͯ dom/CC) 
  					 (reflectsClosedness tforallE ∁ͯC implE (p pfilterE)))❙
❚

// proof fails because some of the morphisms in topology.mmt had to be commented out ❙

view ReflectsClosednessToPreservesCloseness : ?ReflectsClosedness → ?PreservesCloseness =
  include ?TopologyMap❙
  reflectsClosedness = tforallI [D] tforallI [d] implI [p] pfilterI tforallI [d] implI [q]
   						preimageI 
   						(((p pfilterE) tforallE (homX d))
   						implE
   						(bigger_close subset_image_preimage
   							((preservesCloseness tforallE (C preimage homX) d) implE q)))❙
❚

view PreservesClosenessToExpandsClosure : ?PreservesCloseness → ?ExpandsClosure =
  include ?TopologyMap❙
  preservesCloseness = tforallI [D] tforallI [d] implI [p] 
   						subsetE (expandsClosure tforallE D) mapI p❙
❚

view ExpandsClosureToPreimageExpandsInterior : ?ExpandsClosure → ?PreimageExpandsInterior =
  include ?TopologyMap❙
  expandsClosure = _❙
❚

view PreimageExpandsInteriorToReflectsNeighborhood : ?PreimageExpandsInterior → ?ReflectsNeighborhood =
  include ?TopologyMap❙
  preimageExpandsInterior = tforallI [C] subsetI [d,p] pfilterI
  							(reflectsNeighborhood tforallE d tforallE C implE
  							(preimageE p pfilterE))❙
❚

view ReflectsNeighborhoodToReflectsOpenness : ?ReflectsNeighborhood → ?ReflectsOpenness =
  include ?TopologyMap❙
  reflectsNeighborhood = tforallI [d] tforallI [C] implI [p]
  						 p pfilterE texistsE [O,q] pfilterI texistsI (O preimage homX)
  						 andI (andI (reflectsOpenness tforallE O implE (q andEl andEl))
  						 			preimageI (q andEl andEr))
  						 	   subset_preimage (q andEr)❙
❚

theory Continuous = 
  include ?TopologyMap❙

fixmeta latin:/powertypes?PowerSFOL❚

theory Closure =
  include ?ClosureSystem❙
  include ?ClosureOperator❘ = ?ClosureOperatorToClosureSystem❙
  include ?Closeness❘ = ?ClosenessToClosureOperator❙
❚

theory Topology =
  include ?Closure❙
  include ?ClosedTopology❙
  include ?OpenTopology❘ = ?OpenTopologyToClosedTopology❙
  include ?NeighborhoodTopology❘ = ?NeighborhoodTopologyToOpenTopology❙
  include ?InteriorTopology❘ = ?InteriorTopologyToNeighborhoodTopology❙
  // These declarations are semantically correct, but MMT cannot certify that because of a non-trivial equality between morphisms.
     We have the following diagram, where C and T abbreviate Closure and Topology, and i-edges are inclusions from inside to outside.
     The subdiagrams marked // commute by construction, and MMT can exploit that.
     The subdiagram marked //? also commutes, but MMT does not know that.
     The equality is non-trivial because it requires equality reasoning in the object logic (as well as proof irrelevance).
     
     OpenT --------------> ClosedT
        ^                  /i     \
       /              CSystem      \
      /      //?       ^  \    //   \
     /                 |   v         v
NeighborhoodT          |  Closeness-i-CloseT
     ^                 |   /         /
      \                |  v    //   /
       \              COperator    / 
        \                    \i   v
   InteriorT <-------------- ClosureT
  ❙

  // include ?ClosureTopology❘ = ?ClosureTopologyToInteriorTopology❙
  // include ?ClosenessTopology❘ = ?ClosenessTopologyToClosureTopology❙
❚

<content>
namespace latin:/❚

// views between the isomorphic axiomatizations of closure systems/operators:

   ClosureOperator ⟶ ClosureSystem: cl A = intersection of closed supersets of A
   ClosureSystem ⟶ Closeness: A closed if A contains all points close to it
   Closeness ⟶ ClosureOperator: x is close to A if x ∈ cl A  
❚

view ClosureOperatorToClosureSystem : ?ClosureOperator → ?ClosureSystem =
  include ?BaseSet❙  
	closure = [A] ⋂ͯpfilter [C] C ∈ͯ CC ∧ A ⊆ͯ C❙
	extensive_closure = [A] subset_biginter_glb [S,p] p pfilterE andEr❙
	monotone_closure = [A,B,p] subset_biginter pfilterI andI
				 		(intersection_closed subsetI [S,q] q pfilterE andEl)
				 		 subset_biginter_glb [T,r] subset_trans p (r pfilterE andEr)❙
	idempotent_closure = [A] subset_antisym
				 		   (subset_biginter pfilterI andI
				 		   (intersection_closed subsetI [D,p] p pfilterE andEl) subset_refl)
				 		   subset_biginter_glb [S,p] p pfilterE andEr❙
❚

view ClosureSystemToCloseness : ?ClosureSystem → ?Closeness =
  include ?BaseSet❙  
	CC = pfilter [A] ∀ͭ[x] x ⋶ A ⇒ x ∈ͯ A❙
	intersection_closed = [Q,p] pfilterI tforallI [x] implI [q] 
						   biginterI [S,r] subsetE p r pfilterE tforallE x implE
						   bigger_close q subset_biginter r ❙
❚

view ClosenessToClosureOperator : ?Closeness → ?ClosureOperator =
  include ?BaseSet❙  
	close = [x,A] x ∈ͯ cl A❙
	in_close = [x,A,p] subsetE extensive_closure p❙
	bigger_close = [x,A,B,p,q] subsetE (monotone_closure q) p❙
	transitive_close = [A,B,x,p,q] subsetE 
						(subset_trans (monotone_closure (subsetI [y, r] q tforallE y implE r)) 
					 			   	   subset_eq_left idempotent_closure) p❙
❚

// views between the isomorphic axiomatizations of topologies

   ClosedTopology ⟶ ClosenessTopology: A closed if A contains all points close to it
   ClosenessTopology ⟶ ClosureTopology: x is close to A if x ∈ cl A
   ClosureTopology ⟶ InteriorTopology: cl A = complement of the interior of the complement of A
   InteriorTopology ⟶ NeighborhoodTopology: interior A = the set of all x close to A
   NeighborhoodTopology ⟶ OpenTopology: N is a neighborhood of x if there is an open subset O of A
   										  with x ∈ O
   OpenTopology ⟶ ClosedTopology: A is open if its complement is closed
❚

view ClosedTopologyToClosenessTopology : ?ClosedTopology → ?ClosenessTopology =
	include ?ClosureSystemToCloseness❙
	empty_closed = pfilterI tforallI [x] implI [p] empty_union_close notE p inconE❙ 
	finite_union_closed = [A,B,p,q] pfilterI tforallI [x] implI [s] finite_union_close s
						    orE ([l] unionIl (p pfilterE tforallE x implE l))
						         [r] unionIr (q pfilterE tforallE x implE r)❙
❚

view ClosenessTopologyToClosureTopology : ?ClosenessTopology → ?ClosureTopology =
	include ?ClosenessToClosureOperator❙
	empty_union_close = [x] notI [p] emptyE eq_in_left empty_closure p❙
	finite_union_close = [x,A,B,p] unionE (union_closure tcongP ([C] x ∈ͯ C) p)
								           ([l] l orIl) [r] r orIr❙
❚

view ClosureTopologyToInteriorTopology : ?ClosureTopology → ?InteriorTopology =
  include ?BaseSet❙  
	closure = [A] ∁ͯ interior ∁ͯ A ❙
	extensive_closure = [A] subset_trans (subset_eq_right compl_compl) 
										   subset_compl extensive_interior❙
	monotone_closure = [A,B,p] subset_compl monotone_interior subset_compl p❙
	idempotent_closure = [A] compl_compl tsym tcongP ([C] interior C =ͭ interior ∁ͯA) 
					 		(idempotent_interior tsym) tcongT [C] ∁ͯC❙
	empty_closure = compl_empty tsym tcongP ([A] interior A =ͭ fullset) preservation_interior tsym
					tcongP ([A] ∁ͯ A =ͭ ∅ͯ) compl_full❙
	union_closure = [A,B] compl_union tcongT ([C] ∁ͯinterior C) ttrans 
					 (bin_inters_interior tcongT [C] ∁ͯC) ttrans compl_inter❙
❚

view InteriorTopologyToNeighborhoodTopology : ?InteriorTopology → ?NeighborhoodTopology =
  include ?BaseSet❙  
	interior = [A] pfilter [x] x ∶ A❙
	extensive_interior = [A] subsetI [x,p] in_neighborhood (p pfilterE)❙
	idempotent_interior = [A] subset_antisym
	                     		(subsetI [x,p] pfilterI ((openness_neighborhood (p pfilterE)) texistsE [M,q] 
	                     		 superset_closed_neighborhood q tforallE x andEl
	                     		          subsetI [y,r] pfilterI (q tforallE y andEr implE r)))
	                      subsetI [x,p] in_neighborhood (p pfilterE)❙
	bin_inters_interior = [A,B] subset_antisym
							(subsetI [x,p] interI
								(pfilterI superset_closed_neighborhood p pfilterE subset_inter_left)
								 pfilterI superset_closed_neighborhood p pfilterE subset_inter_right)
							 subsetI [x,p] 
							 	pfilterI intersection_closed_neighborhood (interEl p pfilterE) 
															   			   (interEr p pfilterE)❙
	preservation_interior = subset_antisym subset_full subsetI [x,p] pfilterI fullset_neighborhood❙
❚	

view NeighborhoodTopologyToOpenTopology : ?NeighborhoodTopology → ?OpenTopology =
  include ?BaseSet❙
	NN = [x] pfilter [A] ∃ͭ[O] O ∈ͯ OO ∧ x ∈ͯ O ∧ O ⊆ͯ A❙
	nonempty_neighborhood = [x] notI [F] emptyE (F tcongP ([u] fullset ∈ͯ u)
							 pfilterI texistsI fullset andI (andI full_open fullI) subset_refl) ❙
	in_neighborhood = [x,N,p] p pfilterE texistsE [u,q] subsetE q andEr (q andEl andEr)❙
	superset_closed_neighborhood = [M,N,x,p,q] p pfilterE texistsE [u,r] pfilterI texistsI u
						 			andI r andEl subset_trans r andEr q❙
	intersection_closed_neighborhood = [M,N,x,p,q] p pfilterE texistsE [u,r] q pfilterE texistsE [V,s] 
											pfilterI texistsI (u ∩ͯ V) 
												andI (andI 
												(finite_intersection_open r andEl andEl (s andEl andEl)) 
												interI r andEl andEr (s andEl andEr))
											subset_inter_glb
												(subset_trans subset_inter_left (r andEr))
												subset_trans subset_inter_right (s andEr)❙
	openness_neighborhood = [N,x,p] p pfilterE texistsE [u,r] texistsI u tforallI [y]
	            				andI (pfilterI texistsI u andI r andEl subset_refl)
	            					 implI [q] pfilterI texistsI u andI (andI r andEl andEl q) 
	            					 									 (r andEr)❙
❚

view OpenTopologyToClosedTopology : ?OpenTopology → ?ClosedTopology =
  include ?BaseSet❙  
	OO = pfilter [A] ∁ͯ A ∈ͯ CC❙
	full_open = pfilterI (compl_full tsym tcongP ([A] A ∈ͯ CC) empty_closed)❙
	union_open = [Q,p] pfilterI (compl_bigunion tsym tcongP ([u] u ∈ͯ CC) 
				   intersection_closed subsetI [B,q] compl_compl tcongP ([u] u ∈ͯ CC) 
				   (subsetE p (q pfilterE) pfilterE))❙
	finite_intersection_open = [A,B,p,q] pfilterI 
								(compl_inter tsym tcongP ([u] u ∈ͯ CC) 
								 finite_union_closed p pfilterE (q pfilterE))❙
❚

</content>
</file>
